source.title: Precise analysis of ridge interpolators under heavy correlations -- a Random Duality Theory view

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: It analyzes test prediction risk across a feature-to-sample ratio in linear regression, addressing general double descent with a different analytical method and model class from deep networks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical risk characterizations and risk curves for GLS, ridge, and least-squares estimators. The plotted values are not tabulated, so figure-only results are recorded as such. It also shows a null-risk reference, but does not give its plotted numerical value. Double-descent results cited from other studies are not recorded as this paper's results.
record.test_reason: The paper derives closed-form prediction risk for the GLS minimum-norm interpolator, ridge and least squares in correlated Gaussian linear regression. It checks these against simulations (n = 600) across the feature-to-sample ratio 1/α, so its results bear on V4 in a non-deep model class.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that RDT gives exact closed-form risk for the GLS, LS and ridge estimators under full row and column correlations. They say these recover the known double-descent non-monotonicity as over-parametrization grows, and match spectral-method results when intra-sample correlations are absent. They add two observations: GLS risk may be U-shaped in the interpolating regime depending on SNR, and intra-sample correlation need not raise GLS risk.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses Random Duality Theory to analyze Gaussian correlated linear-regression estimators and their asymptotic prediction risk; it does not reproduce a deep-network experiment or use the original neural-network method.
record.method_sensitivity: Risk also depends on covariance structure; the authors report that increasing intra-sample correlation does not always increase GLS risk in the low-correlation regime (Figure 3).

fits_no_version.finding: At α = 0.5, GLS risk is not always increasing as intra-sample correlation qy increases in the low-correlation regime.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Intra-sample correlation need not monotonically raise interpolator prediction risk in linear regression.

record.problems: The displayed risk values are figures rather than tables, and the paper does not give plotted numerical values or simulation error bars. The simulations use n = 600; the theoretical results are asymptotic.

untested.parts: No sweep of sample count with features fixed is reported separately.
Only linear regression estimators. No other model classes.
No noise sweep and no optimally tuned regularization test. Ridge λ is unreported.

missing.what: Closed-form LS risk σ̄²/(α−1), which diverges as α→1 at the interpolation threshold. This is the analytic basis of the peak.
Statement that GLS risk may show a U-shape in the interpolating regime 1/α > 1, depending on SNR.
Null-risk reference curve in Figures 1–2, the comparison for whether overparameterized risk beats the trivial predictor.

record.verdict_notes: This is a methodological, theoretical paper. The double-descent shape in isotropic linear regression was already established (Hastie et al., Belkin–Hsu–Xu), and the paper reproduces it. Its novelty is handling correlations. All curve evidence is figure-only, with no tabulated values or error bars. Ridge λ is never stated, so the ridge rows can't speak to V6.

versions.untested_parts: Deep networks are not studied; the subjects are linear regression estimators.
No sample-count sweep with feature count fixed; the reported sweep is over the feature-to-sample ratio.
The tested class is correlated linear regression, not a broad survey of model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as a predictor of peak location across axes.
No controlled noise sweep, test of multiple peaks, or test of disappearance under optimally tuned regularization.
No re-counting of complexity by an effective parameter count.

rows.subject: GLS interpolator
rows.operation_detail: Prediction risk plotted across the feature-to-sample ratio; the horizontal axis is 1/α, with α = m/n.
rows.note: The figure shows theoretical and simulated risk curves. The paper describes the GLS interpolating risk as exhibiting double descent; plotted numerical values are not tabulated.
rows.check: The text states the GLS interpolating risk 'exhibits the double-descent'. The value is figure-only.

rows.subject: Ridge reg
rows.operation_detail: Prediction risk plotted across the feature-to-sample ratio; the horizontal axis is 1/α, with α = m/n.
rows.note: The figure shows theoretical and simulated risk curves for ridge regression. The text reports non-monotonic risk behavior for the studied estimators; plotted numerical values are not tabulated.
rows.check: The text never says ridge risk shows a peak or double descent, and λ is not stated. The row can't be read as a double-descent curve. It could bear on V6 (regularization removes the peak), but λ is not tuned or reported.

rows.subject: LS
rows.operation_detail: Prediction risk plotted across the feature-to-sample ratio; the horizontal axis is 1/α, with α = m/n.
rows.note: The figure shows theoretical and simulated risk curves for least squares. The text reports non-monotonic risk behavior for the studied estimators; plotted numerical values are not tabulated.
rows.check: LS is defined only in the under-parameterized regime (1/α < 1). Its risk σ̄²/(α−1) (Corollary 1) shows only the ascent toward the interpolation threshold, not a second descent.

rows.subject: GLS interpolator
rows.operation_detail: Prediction risk plotted across the feature-to-sample ratio; the horizontal axis is 1/α, with α = m/n.
rows.note: The figure shows theoretical and simulated risk curves with correlated rows of X. Numerical values are not tabulated.
rows.check: Row-correlated X version. The GLS results carry over with σ̄ redefined (eq. 130). The value is figure-only.

rows.subject: Ridge reg.
rows.operation_detail: Prediction risk plotted across the feature-to-sample ratio; the horizontal axis is 1/α, with α = m/n.
rows.note: The figure shows theoretical and simulated risk curves with correlated rows of X. Numerical values are not tabulated.
rows.check: Same issue as F1-Ridge: λ is unstated and the text makes no claim about the shape of the ridge curve.

rows.subject: LS
rows.operation_detail: Prediction risk plotted across the feature-to-sample ratio; the horizontal axis is 1/α, with α = m/n.
rows.note: The figure shows theoretical and simulated risk curves with correlated rows of X. Numerical values are not tabulated.
rows.check: Covers only the under-parameterized side of the threshold. It shows the rise toward the peak but no second descent.

rows.subject: GLS interpolator
rows.operation_detail: Prediction risk measured as the intra-sample correlation coefficient qy varies.
rows.note: The authors state that in the low intra-sample-correlation regime, risk does not always increase as correlation increases. This is about correlation dependence, not one of the listed claim versions.
rows.check: Measures how risk depends on intra-sample correlation at fixed α = 0.5. This is not a capacity sweep, so it bears on no version.

relationships.condition: GLS minimum-norm interpolator in correlated Gaussian linear regression, with and without row correlations (Figures 1–2)
relationships.reason: The text states GLS risk shows double descent in 1/α, and theory matches simulation; the LS side shows the ascent toward the threshold (F1-GLS, F2-GLS, F1-LS, F2-LS).
relationships.display_finding: GLS risk showed double descent as 1/α varied, with theory matching simulations, while least-squares results showed the ascent toward interpolation.

relationships.condition: GLS interpolating regime (1/α > 1), depending on SNR
relationships.reason: From the text, not the rows: GLS risk can turn U-shaped again past the interpolation point, depending on SNR (σ). So the second descent is not always monotone (F1-GLS, F2-GLS).
relationships.display_finding: Risk could become U-shaped again beyond interpolation, making the second descent nonmonotonic depending on signal-to-noise ratio.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
